selection_rule: An award notice is entered when its buyer is a ledger organisation and a supplier named on the award is a ledger organisation, the award is dated from 1 January 2019 to the end of record (10 November 2026) and is active, and the ledger does not already hold the notice. Names are entered only where a research hand judged the published name to be the ledger organisation, its UK arm or a subsidiary carrying its name.

rulings.note: Where two ledger records carry the same name, the supervisor chose one: Ministry of Defence -> mod (the record the ledger's awards and meetings use); Google -> google rather than google-google-deepmind (Google Cloud is not DeepMind); Northrop Grumman -> northrop-grumman; Anduril Industries Inc -> anduril-industries and Anduril Industries UK Limited -> anduril-industries-uk-ltd, as the ledger's existing contract records do. A hand still judges every published name against the chosen record.
rulings.pairs_note: The ledger's Compass comes from one self-reported LinkedIn role and is not established as the catering group Compass Group, so the hand's 'same' is not taken. The ledger's 'Serco, Inc' is the group's US company, held from one LinkedIn role in 2007-2008; Serco Limited is the group's UK company, a sibling and not the same entity, so the hands' 'same' is not taken. The ledger's 'Crown' is the Penguin Random House imprint; Crown Commercial Service, the Crown Estate, the Crown Prosecution Service and the firms named Crown are not it, so those pairs are ruled different without a hand.
